c1: /drift counts every hit on a plugin's skills as retired, even for plugins that are enabled, so those hits never show in the summary. Hits on personal skills are fine.
c2: /drift drops hits on skills of my enabled plugins from the summary as retired. It is not all of them: a plugin installed from a marketplace with the same name as the plugin still shows up.
c3: `pile.py replaced` reports every plugin from a marketplace that still lists it as an orphan to uninstall, and it dies with a KeyError on installs whose marketplace has no listing at all.
c4: find-test on a suite larger than the choice cap never offers the first test of each batch of tests. In a 600-test suite the tests at positions 0, 250 and 500 are never shown, and each batch is one test short.
c5: A suite with exactly as many tests as one choice can hold (250) is not offered whole. find-test splits it into groups and asks which group to look in, as if it were bigger than the cap.
c6: When find-test keeps several groups from a big suite, the shortlist can come out longer than one choice can hold, and the next question built from it is rejected for having too many options.
c7: The stop guard blocks every stop in an unattended implement run, including a plain report of finished work. Its output shows block: true with a score of 0.0.
c8: The stop guard blocks the agent when it stops to ask for the go-ahead to merge, which is an allowed stop. The more clearly the message asks for something allowed, the higher the block score climbs.
c9: `pile.py status` lists every changed upstream file as unmapped. No file attaches to any skill or mechanism it feeds, even though the feeds table names a directory for it.
c10: find-test on a big suite asks about groups labelled "part 1 of 1", and a group of 251 to 500 tests is offered whole as one oversized choice instead of being cut into parts.
